[[File:snime-1.svg|thumb|right|link=|lo snime klina vlaste]]
*this dictionary lists only basic words. Lojban is a live and dynamic language and accumulates more words over time.
*examples are provided only for most useful places of verbs. People in their speech may mention places of verbs not listed here. Feel free to consult them on the meaning of them.
*if there are, for example, 5 places of a verb it doesn't mean you need to remember them all. Not all of them are always needed. Practice will allow you to gradually internalize them while speaking to Lojbanists in real time.
*some examples represent advanced style. I added them to show different (sometimes more powerful) applications of a word. You may try to analyze them later.
==Types of places==
Each place in Lojban can contain one of the following:
*clause
*entity or text
*number
==Situations==
1. an ''entity'' place in a noun matches an ''entity'' place of the main verb:
{{gl|plise|x1 (entity) is an apple of species x2}}
{{gl|grute|x1 (entity) is a fruit of plant x2}}
{{mu|lo plise cu grute|Apple is a fruit.}}
Here the first place of '''plise''' is an entity and it matches the first place of '''grute''' which is also an entity.

2. a ''clause'' place in a noun matches a ''clause'' place of the main verb.

It means that the place is filled either with a clause or another place of ''event'' type:
{{gl|djica|x1 wants x2 (clause)}}
{{gl|nitcu|x1 needs x2 (clause)}}
{{gl|se nitcu|x1 (clause) is needed by x2}}
{{mu|mi djica lo se nitcu|I want what is needed.}}
Here the second place of '''djica''' is a clause and it matches the second place of '''nitcu''' which is also a clause.
{{gl|nicte|x1 (event) is a nighttime}}
{{mu|lo nicte cu nu lo solri na te gusni|Nighttime is when the Sun isn't shining.}}
{{gl|crisa|x1 (event) is a summer}}
{{gl|citsi|x1 (event) is a season}}
{{mu|lo crisa cu citsi}}

3. an ''entity'' place in a noun is vague when put into a ''clause'' place of the main verb.
Putting an entity place into a clause place denotes an obvious relation:
{{mu|mi djica lo plise|I want an apple.}}
The second place of '''djica''' is a clause. Thus '''lo plise''', ''an apple'' plays some role in that clause. Probably it means:
{{mu|mi djica lo nu mi citka lo plise|I want to eat an apple.}}
but may be I just want to hold an apple in my hand. If you need vagueness or just lazy to say more you can use this method.

{{mu|mi lerci|I'm late.}}
probably means that e.g. my arrival happened late.

This is also called "raising" in English.

4. a ''clause'' place in a noun can be put into an ''entity'' place of the main verb:
{{mu|mi klama lo nu penmi|I go to a meeting.}}
The second place of '''klama''' denotes a place where you go. '''lo nu penmi''' denotes a process of meeting, thus we assume that here it is bound to some location where I go.

Another example:
{{mu|lo ka kucli pu catra lo mlatu|Curiosity killed the cat.}}
Here ''curiosity'' is turned into an entity that is able to kill. As it's a clause with '''ka''' it has to refer to some place. As the definition of '''catra''' says nothing about such situation we assume that it refers to the first unfilled place: here it's x2. Thus, it's the curiosity of the cat that killed it.

This situation is also called "lowering" in English.

4. ''text'' place is filled with quotes and start with '''zo''', '''lu ... li'u''', '''zoi''', '''zo'oi''' or some other particles.

5. Numbers are marked with '''li'''

A number specified with '''li''' goes there:
{{mu|ti mitre li mu|This is 5 meters long.}}
or a "number" place from another verb: '''lo namcu''', '''lo se mitre'''.

6. ''property'' is a special kind of clause. It contains a '''ce'u''' particle:
*When used in the first place of the verb '''ce'u''' refers to the second place of the verb.
*When used in the another place of the verb '''ce'u''' refers to the first place of the verb.
*If explicitly specified in the definition then it refers to what is described in the definition.

{{gl|ckaji|x1 (infinitive of x2) is a property of x2}}
{{mu|lo ka kukte cu ckaji lo badna|Bananas are characterized as being sweet.|Being tasty is a property of bananas.}}
{{mu|mi kakne lo ka limna|I am able to swim.}}


Some properties can refer equally to several places:
{{mu|mi zmadu do lo ka clani vau lo centre be li mu|I am 5 centimeters taller than you.|I am more than you in length by 5 centimeters.}}
{{gl|zmadu|x1 (any type) exceeds or is more than x2 (any type) in x3 (property of x1 and x2 with {kau}) by amount x4}}
Here, '''mi''' and '''do''' are compared, and '''ce'u''' in the third place refers to each of them equally.

7. ''proposition'' is a place filled with '''du'u'''. It works exactly as '''nu''' but is traditionally used with some places and always mentioned for them in the dictionary:
{{gl|djuno|x1 (entity) knows that x2 (proposition) is true}}
{{mu|mi djuno lo du'u do stati|I know that you are smart.}}

8. Instead of ''property'' you may use another type of clause with '''nu''' or '''du'u'''. Compare
{{mu|mi djica lo ka sipna|I want to sleep.}}
{{mu|mi djica lo nu do sipna|I want you to sleep.|I want that you sleep.}}

{{notci|In case of doubt with places open the dictionary and look at the examples. At least one of the usage examples will have all places filled.}}
